steps: Bring the whole milk and about 1 1/4 cups of water to a gentle simmer in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the rolled oats and the cinnamon, stirring for 5-7 minutes until creamy.
Slice the banana into rounds.
Transfer the oatmeal to a bowl and top with the blueberries and banana slices.
Top with the granola and strawberries, then drizzle with the honey and maple syrup.

note: Cooking-liquid fix: 80 g dry oats needs ~3x its weight in liquid, so step 1 now simmers the milk with about 1 1/4 cups of water. Per SPEC bug-class 2 the liquid is step-text only, NOT added to ingredients (the report had proposed Water 300 g as an ingredient). Added Cinnamon 1 g (recipe had no spice row). Left the Honey + Maple Syrup pair alone - the report marked that consolidation purely cosmetic and optional.
clean, no change - verdict was `coherent` and the report proposed no fix (the milk 40 g -> 20 g note was an explicit non-requirement).

steps: Toast the whole wheat bread slices until golden.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water until the whites are just set.
Mash the avocado with a fork, squeeze in the lemon juice, and season with salt, black pepper, and chili flakes.
Spread the mashed avocado on the toast and top with the poached eggs.

note: Added Lemon 10 g - the acid finish is the one real composition gap in avocado toast. Phantom-fat fix taken via the zero-cost route the report recommended: step 2 is now poach-only instead of 'fry or poach', so no oil is needed. Spices unchanged.

steps: Blend the rolled oats into a flour in a blender.
Add the eggs, mashed banana, greek yogurt, baking powder, cinnamon, and a splash of whole milk to the blender and mix until smooth.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and melt the butter to grease it.
Pour batter to form 3 pancakes and cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Stack the pancakes and top with the granola, blueberries, and strawberries, then drizzle with the maple syrup.

note: Phantom-fat fix: added Butter 5 g (+36 cal) and step 3 now melts it instead of saying 'lightly grease'. Added Baking Powder (leavening - the batter had nothing to lift it) and Cinnamon; recipe previously had no spice row. Baking Powder set to 3 g not the report's 4 g to stay inside SPEC's 0.5-3 g spice band.

steps: Peel and freeze the banana in advance for best results.
Blend the frozen banana, blueberries, greek yogurt, and a splash of whole milk until thick and creamy.
Pour into a bowl.
Top with the granola, rolled oats, mango, and strawberries, then drizzle with the honey and maple syrup.
Serve immediately before it melts.

note: Macro-neutral step fix: the 30 g of dry rolled oats moved out of the cold blend (raw oats never hydrate there - they go gritty and the bowl stiffens, contradicting 'serve immediately') and into the topping alongside the granola. Ingredients and grams untouched; sweetener consolidation left alone as optional/cosmetic.

steps: Whisk together the eggs, whole milk, cinnamon, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt in a shallow dish.
Dip the bread slices in the custard, soaking each side for 20-30 seconds.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat.
Cook the bread slices 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve topped with the sliced strawberries, blueberries, sliced banana, granola, and rolled oats. Drizzle with the maple syrup.

note: Macro-neutral coherence fix: crushed rolled oats removed from the egg custard (French toast is defined by bread absorbing a LIQUID custard; 20 g of dry oats made a slurry that coats and scorches) and moved to the topping - same grams. Added Vanilla Extract 2 g and Salt 0.5 g to the spice row, and lengthened the soak from 10 s to 20-30 s per side now that the custard is thin.

steps: Season the pork loin with salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika, then slice it thinly.
Heat the olive oil in a hot pan and sear the pork for 2-3 minutes per side.
Warm the whole wheat tortilla in a dry pan or microwave for 15 seconds.
Slice the avocado and the tomato.
Layer the seared pork on the tortilla, then add the spinach, avocado, and tomato.
Roll up tightly, tucking in the sides. Slice in half and serve.

note: Route (A), the report's recommendation: renamed off 'Club' rather than rebuilding it into one. A club is poultry + bacon + tomato + lettuce + mayo; this was pork, tortilla, avocado, spinach - four of the five defining parts missing - so the honest fix is the name. Phantom-fat fix: added Olive Oil 5 g for the sear (pork loin is ~5% fat and renders nothing). Added Tomato 50 g for moisture across a dry 270 g wrap, and Smoked Paprika to the rub. About +54 cal; stays high-protein/low-fat.

steps: Season the chicken breast with salt, black pepper, and garlic powder.
Grill or pan-sear the chicken 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through, then let it rest and slice.
Wash and chop the romaine lettuce.

Whisk the mayonnaise with the lemon juice, worcestershire sauce, a pinch of garlic powder, a little of the olive oil, and half the parmesan cheese into a smooth dressing, then toss it with the romaine.
Cube the whole wheat bread, toss it with the remaining olive oil, and toast until crisp to make croutons.
Top the salad with the sliced chicken, the remaining shaved parmesan cheese, and the croutons.

note: Kept the name and built an actual Caesar instead. Both defining components were missing: the emulsifier and the savory backbone. Added Mayonnaise 15 g (emulsified yolk/oil/acid - the registry has no yolk entry and whole-egg macros would lie to the solver) and Worcestershire Sauce 5 g. Olive Oil 10 g -> 8 g, now split between dressing and croutons so the croutons are fatted rather than toasted dry, and the garlic powder finally reaches the dressing. Net about +86 cal / +9 g fat, protein unchanged. NOTE: the report asked for Worcestershire Sauce as a spice-override, but Phase A added it to INGREDIENT_REGISTRY with real macros (78 cal, 19.5C), so it is an ingredient here - it is not in the dual-listed spice vocabulary.

steps: Mix the ground beef with the panko breadcrumbs, grated parmesan cheese, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, oregano, dried basil, and a beaten egg, then form into meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in a pan on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through.
Split the whole wheat bread lengthwise into a roll shape and toast lightly.
Fill the toasted bread with the meatballs and sauce.
Top with sliced mozzarella cheese and broil briefly until the cheese melts.

note: Phantom-ingredient fix: steps 4 and 5 named a 'sub roll' the recipe does not have - now they name the Whole Wheat Bread that is actually in the list. Added Oregano and Dried Basil (an Italian-American meatball mix wants them) and Parmesan Cheese 10 g to the mix (+42 cal / +2.8 g protein). Left Egg at 50 g: the report called the 25 g trim optional and not required for coherence, and adjustDayMeals caps binder eggs at their original grams anyway. Cuisine deliberately stays American - the meatball sub is an Italian-American invention that does not exist in Italy; the report asks explicitly that nobody 'fix' it to Italian. Step 2's dry-pan browning is correct (80% lean beef renders its own fat) and is NOT a phantom-fat case.

steps: Season and grill or pan-sear the chicken breast until cooked through, then dice.
Hard-boil the egg for 10 minutes, then peel and quarter it.
Fry the bacon until very crisp, drain it on paper towel, and crumble.
Dice the avocado and the tomato.
Chop the romaine lettuce and arrange it on a plate.
Arrange rows of chicken, egg, avocado, tomato, crumbled bacon, and crumbled blue cheese on the lettuce.
Whisk the olive oil with the red wine vinegar, salt, and black pepper into a vinaigrette, drizzle it over the salad, and scatter with sliced green onion.

note: Both tiers applied - Phase A put Blue Cheese and Bacon in the registry, which unblocks tier 2. Tier 1: added Tomato 60 g, Green Onion 10 g (stand-in for the canonical chives, same allium family), and Red Wine Vinegar 8 g so the bare drizzle of oil becomes an actual vinaigrette. Tier 2: Cheddar Cheese 20 g -> Blue Cheese 20 g (the Cobb's signature flavor; no source treats cheddar as a variant) and Bacon 20 g crisped and crumbled. The composed-rows technique was already correct and is preserved. About +96 cal / +8 g fat. Cheddar Cheese stays in the registry (Scrambled Eggs & Toast still uses it); Bacon is already in the MEAT_INGREDIENTS Set at index.html:438, so no set edit is needed.

steps: Season the pork shoulder generously with salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika.
Place it in a slow cooker or Dutch oven with about half a cup of water and cover tightly.
Cook on low for 3 hours until fork-tender.
Shred the pork with two forks and toss it with the BBQ sauce.
Split the whole wheat bread lengthwise into a roll shape and toast lightly.
Toss the coleslaw mix with the red wine vinegar and a pinch of salt and black pepper, then pile the pork on the bread and top with the slaw.

note: Route (A) - fix the dish, now that Phase A added Pork Shoulder to the registry. You cannot pull Pork Loin: shredding depends on collagen melting to gelatin, and 3 hours of low-and-slow on a lean low-collagen cut dries it into strings. Swapping to shoulder makes every step true. Also fixed the phantom 'sub rolls' (steps 5-6 now name the Whole Wheat Bread), named the braising liquid in the step text, and dressed the slaw with Red Wine Vinegar - undressed bagged cabbage is not coleslaw, and a vinegar slaw is both the zero-macro option and the idiomatic eastern-NC pairing. Macro shift is much smaller than the report feared: the registry's Pork Shoulder is 186 cal/17.7P/12.4F per 100 g, not the ~270 estimated, so at 150 g this is about +65 cal, -12 g protein, +13 g fat (~470 -> ~535 cal). Still protein-dense at ~26% of calories, so the high-protein tag holds. Per SPEC bug-class 2, Water is named in the step but NOT added to ingredients (the report had proposed Water 120 g as an ingredient). Pork Loin stays in the registry - Pork & Avocado Wrap still uses it. Pork Shoulder is already in the MEAT_INGREDIENTS Set at index.html:438, so no set edit is needed.

steps: Dice the turkey breast small.
Heat the sesame oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook the diced onion, garlic, and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the turkey and cook 4-5 minutes until golden, seasoning with salt, black pepper, and white pepper.
Add the soy sauce and hoisin sauce and toss to glaze in the last minute.
Grate or julienne the carrot into thin strips.
Separate the butter lettuce leaves to use as cups.
Fill the lettuce cups with the turkey and carrot, scatter with the sliced green onion, and squeeze the lime over the top.

note: Cuisine relabelled American -> Chinese: this is san choy bow, a Cantonese dish; soy-glazed minced meat in lettuce cups reads American only by venue. Chinese already exists as a label (was 2 recipes), so no new label is needed. Added the missing flavor spine - Sesame Oil 5 g, Garlic 6 g, Ginger 6 g, Hoisin Sauce 15 g, Green Onion 15 g, all already in the registry - and moved the Onion from a raw side garnish (incoherent next to a mild hot filling) to a cooked aromatic. Romaine Lettuce 80 g -> Butter Lettuce 80 g: romaine leaves are long, flat and stiffly ribbed and will not cup, and Phase A added Butter Lettuce to the registry precisely for this (it is currently referenced by no recipe, so this also clears a would-be orphan). Kept Lime. About +95 cal / +9 g carbs / +5 g fat on a small ~300 cal recipe; total carbs land near 24 g so the low-carb tag still holds. Romaine Lettuce stays in the registry (Caesar and Cobb use it).

_summary.macroDeltas: measured against the live registry: Classic Oatmeal 683->683 (0%), Avocado Toast 427->430 (+0.7%), Protein Pancakes 711->747 (+5.0%), Smoothie Bowl 668->668 (0%), French Toast 653->653 (0%), Pork&Avocado Wrap 448->501 (+11.9%), Chicken Caesar 533->621 (+16.5%), Meatball Sub 857->896 (+4.6%), Cobb Salad 569->665 (+16.8%), Pulled Pork 471->535 (+13.7%, protein 46.9->34.5 - the only meaningful protein drop in the slice), Turkey Lettuce Wraps 304->397 (+30.4%). Turkey Lettuce Wraps is the one recipe past SPEC's +/-25% guideline; the report justifies it line-by-line (sesame oil +45, hoisin +33, aromatics +15) and the cause is that the dish started at only 304 cal, which is small for the solver anyway. Protein is unchanged or up everywhere except Pulled Pork.
_summary.notes: Full scope applied including both Cobb tiers and Pulled Pork route (A) - Phase A had already added Blue Cheese, Bacon, Pork Shoulder and Butter Lettuce to the registry, which unblocked every fix the report had marked as needing a new entry. No new cuisine label is introduced by this slice (Chinese already exists, going 2 -> 3 recipes). Bacon and Pork Shoulder are ALREADY in the MEAT_INGREDIENTS Set at index.html:438 - I verified; no set edit needed. Nothing is orphaned: Cheddar Cheese leaves Cobb but stays in Scrambled Eggs & Toast, Pork Loin leaves Pulled Pork but stays in Pork & Avocado Wrap, Romaine Lettuce leaves Turkey Lettuce Wraps but stays in Caesar and Cobb. Butter Lettuce goes 0 -> 1 recipe, clearing a Phase A orphan. Scrambled Eggs & Toast is the slice's only no-change record. No nut, olive or Sumac was needed anywhere - the hard constraints never bound. Two Red Wine Vinegar spice entries are 8 g and 10 g, above SPEC's 0.5-3 g band: deliberate, since CLAUDE.md routes zero-macro liquid seasonings through RECIPE_SPICE_OVERRIDES and the existing data.js Red Wine Vinegar entry is already 10 g.
